source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

notes: Stephen gives the family total as seventy-five, following the Greek form of the ancestral story. The translation does not harmonize this with the Hebrew total of seventy.
Stephen compresses details associated with the ancestral burials and the purchase at Shechem. The translation follows his speech rather than silently reconciling it with Genesis.
The word translated ‘assembly’ is the same term often rendered ‘church’; here it refers to Israel gathered in the wilderness.
Moloch and Rephan are names in Stephen’s quotation of the prophets. The exact ancient identifications are not explained in the main text.
‘Uncircumcised in heart and ears’ is a prophetic image for stubborn resistance, not a statement about physical disability.
vocabulary: Covenant, an established binding relationship or arrangement.
Redeemer or liberator, one who brings release.

notes: Simon’s belief and baptism are narrated, but Peter exposes his attempt to buy divine authority. The account does not invite readers to treat the Spirit as a commodity.
The Greek uses the vivid images ‘gall of bitterness’ and ‘bond of injustice.’ The main text communicates their moral force without turning them into a medical diagnosis.
The traveler is both an Ethiopian court official and a eunuch. The translation preserves these identities rather than reducing him to his occupation.
Verse 37 is absent from the pinned Greek text, so the public verse numbering moves from 36 to 38.
vocabulary: Eunuch; a man whose embodied and social status could be associated with royal service.

notes: ‘The Way’ is an early name for the Jesus-following movement. Both men and women are explicit targets of Saul’s arrests.
The companions hear the voice but see no one. Later retellings emphasize different aspects of what they perceived; this verse is translated on its own terms.
Saul is chosen to carry Jesus’ name to Gentiles, kings, and Israel, and he is also told that this mission will involve suffering.
Tabitha is Aramaic and Dorcas Greek; both names mean gazelle. She is explicitly called a female disciple.
The widows’ tunics and garments make Dorcas’s care materially visible rather than merely describing her as kind.
vocabulary: Way, road, or manner of life; here a name for the early movement.

notes: A centurion ordinarily commanded about one hundred soldiers; the Italian Cohort identifies Cornelius’s military unit.
Peter’s vision uses food categories, but Peter later states its human implication: he must not call any person defiled or unclean.
Peter describes a serious inherited boundary around association with foreigners, then explicitly attributes its overturning to God.
God’s impartiality is expressed in welcome across nations. The lines do not claim that human merit purchases grace.
The Spirit is poured out before these Gentile hearers are baptized in water, removing the circumcised believers’ stated reason to withhold baptism.
vocabulary: One who shows partiality or judges by status.

notes: The criticism centers on Peter entering the homes of uncircumcised men and eating with them, not merely on his preaching.
Peter says the Spirit told him to go without ‘making distinctions.’ Six fellow believers accompany him as witnesses.
Peter’s question frames resistance to the Gentiles’ reception of the Spirit as standing in God’s way.
The pinned text reads ‘Greek-speaking people,’ a form that can refer to Hellenists; the note does not silently substitute a different textual reading.
The anticipated famine leads the disciples to concrete, ability-based relief for believers in Judea.
vocabulary: Repentance, a changed mind and direction.
Christian, a person identified with Christ.

notes: Herod has James killed with the sword. The narrative states the political violence plainly.
Four squads of four soldiers underline the security around Peter; ‘Passover’ is the festival setting, not a Christian Easter observance.
‘His angel’ is the gathered group’s proposed explanation. The narrator reports it without endorsing a complete theory of guardian angels.
The guards’ removal follows an official examination and carries the threat of execution. The translation names the lethal consequence.
Herod’s death is described graphically as being eaten by worms. The harm is retained without embellishment.
vocabulary: Passover, the festival remembering Israel’s deliverance from Egypt.
Earnestly, fervently, or with sustained intensity.
Bedchamber; by extension, a trusted royal chamberlain or household official.

notes: Manaen’s description indicates that he was raised with or closely associated with Herod the tetrarch; the precise social arrangement is uncertain.
The pinned Greek supports ‘put up with them,’ a difficult description of God’s patience in the wilderness. A closely related textual form can mean ‘carried them.’
The syntax places the approximately 450 years with the preceding sequence before the judges. The main text makes that punctuation choice visible rather than disguising it.
The psalm’s ‘today I have begotten you’ retains a royal birth image. Paul uses the quotation here while announcing God’s fulfillment in raising up Jesus.
‘Appointed to eternal life’ is retained without adding an explanation of how divine appointment and human response relate.
The man’s inability to walk is lifelong, from birth. Person-first language preserves his humanity without hiding the condition.
The crowd identifies Barnabas with Zeus and Paul with Hermes. The apostles reject the honor and insist on their shared humanity.
Rain, fruitful seasons, food, and joy are named as God’s witness in ordinary provision.
The crowd stones Paul and drags him outside the city believing him dead. The narrative records severe collective violence without stating explicitly that he died.
Entry into God’s kingdom through many troubles describes the disciples’ costly path; it does not call the violence against them good.
vocabulary: Empty, futile, or worthless; here describing idols and their worship.
Elder, a recognized leader in a local church.
